title: No Two Values Equally Common
statement:
You get an array nums. Count how many times each distinct value appears.

Return true if no two different values have the same count, and false otherwise.

examples.why: 4 appears 3 times, 7 twice, 9 once. All three counts differ.
2 and 5 both appear twice. It does not matter that the values themselves are different.
Counts 2 and 1. Negative numbers and zero are ordinary values.

hints: First count every value. What do you then need to know about the counts?
You want to know whether the list of counts contains a repeat. That is the same question as 'are these numbers all distinct?'.
Put the counts into a set. If the set is smaller than the number of distinct values, two counts collided.

explain.intuition: The question is about the counts, not the values. So do it in two layers: a map from value to count, then a check that the counts are all different. The second layer is the classic "any duplicates?" check, answered by comparing sizes: new Set(counts).size === counts.length.
steps: Build a map from each value to its count.
Collect the map's counts into a set.
Return whether the set has as many entries as the map.
pitfalls: Checking that the values are distinct instead of their counts.
Using an array indexed by value without shifting negatives, so -1 becomes an invalid index.

solutions.title: Sort, then compare run lengths
solutions.idea: After sorting, equal values sit together. Measure each run's length, sort the lengths and look for neighbours that match.

solutions.title: Count map plus a set of counts
solutions.idea: Count with a map, then check that the counts are all different by putting them in a set.

followups: Return the fewest elements to delete so that all counts become distinct.
The array is a stream. Can you keep the answer up to date after every new element?
